_note: Trivia for star dust. 40 questions in 4 levels of difficulty (10 each). A round asks 10, getting harder. Facts checked against NASA, ESA, ISRO and agency histories; photos are NASA images (see docs/CREDITS.md); art: draws a subject with no suitable photo (sputnik, dsky, mars_orbit, or rocket:<name> from rocket_art.gd). answer is the index of the right choice.

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explain: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969 during Apollo 11. Buzz Aldrin followed him; Michael Collins stayed in orbit.

questions.question: What was the first artificial satellite?
questions.explain: The USSR launched Sputnik 1 on 4 October 1957. It was a polished ball with four antennas that sent out a simple beep.

questions.question: Who was the first human in space?
questions.explain: Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth once in Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.

questions.question: Recognise this rocket.
questions.explain: This is a Saturn V, the rocket that launched the Apollo crews to the Moon. It is still one of the most powerful rockets ever flown.

questions.question: What does ISS stand for?
questions.explain: The International Space Station has had people living on board without a break since November 2000.

questions.question: How many astronauts flew on Apollo 11?
questions.explain: Three: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins. Two landed; Collins orbited the Moon in the command module.

questions.question: Which planet did the Curiosity rover land on in 2012?
questions.explain: Curiosity landed in Gale Crater on Mars in August 2012 and is still exploring.

questions.question: Which space telescope did the Space Shuttle launch in 1990?
questions.explain: The Space Shuttle Discovery released Hubble into orbit in April 1990.

questions.question: Why does a satellite in low orbit need a battery?
choices: To keep working while the Earth blocks the Sun
questions.explain: In low orbit the Earth hides the Sun for a big part of every orbit, and the solar panels make nothing in the dark.

questions.question: What does 1U mean for a CubeSat?
questions.explain: A CubeSat is built from 10 cm cubes. 1U is one cube; a 3U CubeSat is three stacked together.

questions.question: Which country built Aryabhata, its first satellite, in 1975?
questions.explain: Aryabhata was built by India's space agency, ISRO, and launched on a Soviet rocket in April 1975.

questions.question: Who led the MIT team that wrote the on-board flight software for Apollo?
questions.explain: Margaret Hamilton led the software engineering team for the Apollo guidance computer at the MIT Instrumentation Laboratory. Katherine Johnson worked on trajectory calculations at NASA.

questions.question: Which NASA mathematician checked the computer's orbit numbers by hand before John Glenn's 1962 flight?
questions.explain: John Glenn asked for Katherine Johnson to verify the computer's calculations before he flew Friendship 7 in February 1962.

questions.question: What did Explorer 1 discover in 1958?
questions.explain: Explorer 1's radiation counter found belts of charged particles trapped by Earth's magnetic field, now called the Van Allen belts.

questions.question: Recognise this spacecraft.
questions.explain: This is the International Space Station, photographed from the Space Shuttle Endeavour in 2011.

questions.question: What kind of missions did the Saturn V fly?
questions.explain: The Saturn V launched the crewed Apollo missions to the Moon. Its last flight, in 1973, put the Skylab space station into orbit.

questions.question: Recognise this rover.
questions.explain: This is Curiosity, in a selfie taken with the camera on its robotic arm. The arm is left out of the picture because it holds the camera.

questions.question: What protects a capsule when it comes back through the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Hitting the air at many kilometres per second heats the capsule to thousands of degrees. The heat shield takes that heat. The photo shows the heat shield for NASA's Orion capsule being built.

questions.question: Why are satellites shaken on a vibration table before launch?
choices: To check they survive the shaking of launch
questions.explain: A launch shakes a spacecraft hard. Vibration tests find loose parts on the ground, not in orbit.

questions.question: What does a geomagnetic storm do to satellites in very low orbit?
choices: It makes the upper air thicker, so they are dragged down
questions.explain: The storm heats the upper atmosphere, which swells and drags low satellites. In 2022 about 38 new Starlink satellites burned up this way.

questions.question: Why was Mars Climate Orbiter lost in 1999?
questions.explain: One team's software gave thruster data in pound-force seconds; another expected newton-seconds. The orbiter flew too low into Mars' atmosphere.

questions.question: About how long did Sputnik 1 keep transmitting before its batteries died?
questions.explain: Sputnik 1 had no solar panels. Its batteries kept the radio going for about three weeks.

questions.question: Which rocket launched India's Chandrayaan-1 to the Moon in 2008?
questions.explain: Chandrayaan-1 launched on a PSLV, India's workhorse rocket, from Sriharikota in October 2008.

questions.question: These engines are being test-fired for NASA's SLS rocket. What engine type are they?
questions.explain: These are four RS-25 engines, the same type that powered the Space Shuttle, firing during the SLS core stage test at Stennis in 2021.

questions.question: What exploded on Apollo 13 on the way to the Moon?
choices: A fuel tank on the lander
An oxygen tank in the service module
questions.explain: An oxygen tank in the service module exploded. The crew used the lunar module as a lifeboat and came home safely. The photo shows the damaged service module drifting away, taken by the crew.

questions.question: Recognise this part of the Apollo spacecraft.
questions.explain: This is the lunar module Eagle, coming back from the Moon's surface to meet the command module. The Earth is rising behind it.

questions.question: What was wrong with Hubble when it reached orbit?
choices: Its main mirror was the wrong shape
It was in the wrong orbit
questions.explain: The main mirror was ground very slightly to the wrong shape, so pictures were blurry. Astronauts fitted corrective optics in 1993.

questions.question: Which mission sent the first CubeSats to another planet?
questions.explain: The two MarCO CubeSats flew past Mars in 2018 and relayed data from the InSight lander as it landed.

questions.question: What did the Voyager probes carry as a message to anyone who finds them?
questions.explain: Each Voyager carries a gold-plated record of sounds, music and pictures from Earth.

questions.question: Which spacecraft first landed people on the Moon?
questions.explain: The lunar module Eagle landed on 20 July 1969. Columbia was the command module that stayed in orbit.

questions.question: Who was the first woman in space?
questions.explain: Valentina Tereshkova flew Vostok 6 in June 1963 and orbited the Earth 48 times.

questions.question: What caused the Space Shuttle Challenger accident in 1986?
choices: A seal on a booster failed in cold weather
questions.explain: An O-ring seal in a solid rocket booster failed after a very cold night, letting hot gas escape.

questions.question: What damaged Space Shuttle Columbia in 2003?
choices: Foam from the fuel tank hit the wing at launch
questions.explain: A piece of insulating foam hit the left wing during launch and damaged its heat protection. The shuttle broke up on its way home.

questions.question: Which was the first spacecraft to make a soft landing on the Moon?
questions.explain: The Soviet Luna 9 landed softly in February 1966, four months before NASA's Surveyor 1.

questions.question: Which country first landed a spacecraft near the Moon's south pole?
questions.explain: India's Chandrayaan-3 landed near the south pole in August 2023.

questions.question: What was the first rover to drive on another planet?
questions.explain: Sojourner drove on Mars in 1997 with the Mars Pathfinder lander. Lunokhod 1 drove earlier, in 1970, but on the Moon, which is not a planet.

questions.question: Why did Ariane 5's first flight fail in 1996?
choices: Software reused from Ariane 4 hit a number too big for it
questions.explain: Guidance software reused from Ariane 4 tried to store a number too big for its format. Both inertial reference units shut down and the rocket broke up.

questions.question: Who was the first American woman in space?
questions.explain: Sally Ride flew on the Space Shuttle Challenger in June 1983. The photo is the STS-7 crew; Sally Ride is front left.

questions.question: What was the first crewed spacecraft to orbit the Moon?
questions.explain: Apollo 8 orbited the Moon ten times at Christmas 1968 and took the famous Earthrise photo (drawn here).

questions.question: About how fast does the ISS travel?
questions.explain: About 28,000 km/h, so it goes round the Earth roughly every 90 minutes.
